findings.page: PDF p. 34 (printed p. 10) and PDF p. 43 (printed p. 19); counter-evidence at PDF p. 103-104 (printed p. 79-80)
findings.evidence: Fig 1.1 caption (PDF p. 34): "[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] — the schematic is drawn from the documented mechanism ([1P][FACT], Ch 4, Table 4-2), and it is not a screenshot or a measurement". Fig 2.1 caption (PDF p. 43): "[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] — the schematic is drawn from the documented mechanism ([1P][FACT], Ch 4)". But Table 4-2 (PDF p. 103-104) labels exactly the geometry these figures draw as scenario assumptions: "Attention architecture | full-MHA reference model (K/V width = hidden_dim) | [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]" and "Reference geometry — layers (n_layers) | 80 | [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] constructed teaching geometry, not a named vendor model".
findings.issue: Provenance-label mismatch: both figure captions cite '[1P][FACT]' and point at Ch 4/Table 4-2 for a geometry that Table 4-2 labels [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] (the only [1P][FACT] rows in Table 4-2 are the H100 hardware constants). Fig 1.1's caption goes further and asserts "the canonical model has 64 query and 64 KV heads per layer (Ch 4, Table 4-2)" — a constructed teaching geometry being presented as a first-party vendor fact. Under the book's own three-axis rule (Preface: provenance = where the number came from; a vendor hardware constant is [1P][FACT], a constructed reference geometry is [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]), this mislabels the scenario baseline as first-party.
findings.fix_instruction: In the Fig 1.1 and Fig 2.1 captions, replace '([1P][FACT], Ch 4, Table 4-2)' / '([1P][FACT], Ch 4)' with the correct provenance for the drawn geometry — e.g. '([canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION], Ch 4, Table 4-2)' for the 80-layer/8,192-hidden/64-head geometry, reserving '[1P][FACT]' for the documented KV-cache mechanism (e.g. the DeepSeek-V2 MLA report, arXiv:2405.04434, and the H100 datasheet already cited elsewhere). Add a one-clause note to the Fig 1.1 caption that the 64-head geometry is the book's constructed teaching baseline, not a vendor checkpoint.
